## Summary

This call was warm, empathetic, and there were moments where Aanchal stayed in the conversation. But the sale was lost because the call lacked control, the offer was presented too broadly, price was pre-justified, and Jessica’s real concern — “I am exhausted, over-invested, and unsure I even want to keep scaling this service business” — was never fully isolated.

Total score: **41/80 — 🔻 Weak/Inconsistent**

The biggest money leak: Jessica did not need more explanation. She needed leadership, clarity, and a grounded decision conversation.

## Scorecard

| Domain | Score |
|---|---:|
| Authority & Presence | 10/20 |
| Clarity & Plan Presentation | 11/20 |
| Urgency & Decision Guidance | 10/20 |
| Pricing Delivery & Objection Handling | 10/20 |
| **Total** | **41/80** |

| Domain | Statement | Score |
|---|---|---:|
| Authority & Presence | Certainty at open | 2 🔻 |
| Authority & Presence | No over-credentialing | 4 ⚡ |
| Authority & Presence | Certainty transferred | 2 🔻 |
| Authority & Presence | Command of conversation | 2 🔻 |
| Clarity & Plan | Simple recommendation | 3 ⚠ |
| Clarity & Plan | Transformation first | 2 🔻 |
| Clarity & Plan | Clinical/process minimalism | 3 ⚠ |
| Clarity & Plan | Clear next step | 3 ⚠ |
| Urgency & Decision | Asked for commitment | 2 🔻 |
| Urgency & Decision | Stayed in room | 4 ⚡ |
| Urgency & Decision | Urgency tied to goals | 2 🔻 |
| Urgency & Decision | Managed emotional energy | 2 🔻 |
| Pricing & Objections | Pricing confidence | 3 ⚠ |
| Pricing & Objections | No pre-justification | 1 ❌ |
| Pricing & Objections | Explored “think about it” | 3 ⚠ |
| Pricing & Objections | Held plan under price pressure | 3 ⚠ |

This grading follows the consult scorecard principle that strong sales calls require certainty, one clear recommendation, a direct ask, and deep objection exploration. fileciteturn0file2

## 🟢 What You Did Well

You did stay with her when she hesitated.

Quote: **“I have the full hour for you. Would you be interested in a monthly payment option or financing?”**

That was strong. You did not immediately run away when she said she could not afford it.

You also named the real business issue at one point.

Quote: **“You cannot be upselling every single client, you cannot be doing all the sales. Right. You need your team to step in.”**

That was the right direction. Jessica’s pain was not just leads. It was operational exhaustion.

## 🔴 Top 3 Conversion Killers

### 1. You opened without authority

Quote: **“Please just go ahead and tell me a bit about yourself and why you booked the call with us today.”**

Why it cost you: she immediately had to lead the call. She was already overwhelmed. Asking her to explain everything from scratch reinforced that nobody had a clear plan for her.

Replacement script:

“Jessica, based on what you shared before the call, it sounds like you are not just looking for more leads. You are looking for a cleaner system that helps you reactivate past clients, automate follow-up, and take pressure off you as the owner. So today I’m going to understand where the biggest revenue leak is, show you exactly where we can help, and then we’ll decide together if this is the right move.”

### 2. You explained the offer, but did not anchor it to her transformation

Quote: **“So if you would hire us, we start off by doing a market blueprint… We then do a revenue leak audit… we try to help you implement your SOPs…”**

Why it cost you: this sounded like services. Jessica needed relief. She needed to hear: “You stop being the bottleneck. Your 6,000-client database starts producing revenue. Your team sells without you.”

Replacement script:

“The goal here is not just ads or AI. The goal is that within 90 days, your old client list is being reactivated, every lead is followed up with automatically, your staff has a clearer sales process, and you are no longer carrying the whole business on your back. That is what we are building.”

### 3. You weakened the price before she responded

Quote: **“I know that a lot of people have a dollar shock when they hear that amount, but we do have a guarantee in place.”**

Why it cost you: you told her the price was scary before she said it was scary. That signals insecurity. The rubric is clear here: state the investment, then stop talking. fileciteturn0file2

Replacement script:

“The investment for the 90-day done-for-you partnership is $15,000.”

Then silence.

When she says she is spent:

“I hear you. And I believe you. So let’s separate two things. Is the concern that you do not believe this can create the return, or is it that the cash flow structure feels too heavy right now?”

## 🎯 The One Thing Drill

Practice this every day before calls:

Say the price in one sentence, then stop.

“The investment is $15,000.”

No explaining. No guarantee. No financing. No softening. Let the prospect respond first.

Want to role-play any of these moments so you can practice the response live?
